candidates.title: Stream crossings and trail mud after rain

River levels after rain were not accounted for here.

Shape: backcountry
Leaving from: Québec City
Going to: Parc national de la Gaspésie
Dates: 3 nights somewhere between 2027-08-15 and 2027-09-15
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: 34, 36
Access needs: not answered
Budget: shoestring, as a feeling rather than a figure
Appetite for effort: demanding
Roughest night they will accept: rustic
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that requires a river ford above the knee

About this backcountry:
Nights away from a road: 3
Shelter: hut
Most they will walk in a day: 16 km
Experience: some
In their words: We have done hut-to-hut in the Chic-Chocs once before, in fair weather. Neither of us has navigated in cloud and we would rather not learn on this trip.

candidates.title: Drive along the St. Lawrence south shore to the Gaspésie park gateway
candidates.summary: The main approach leg, roughly 450 km via Autoroute 20 and Route 132, then Route 299 inland from Sainte-Anne-des-Monts. A stop at Rimouski or Matane breaks it up. The duration is not measured here. Fuel cost is a rough band for one car shared by two. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidates.title: Return drive from the park to the city
candidates.summary: The same corridor in reverse, which is useful as a buffer if cloud cuts the hut route short. The duration is not measured. Fuel is a band for the shared car.

candidates.summary: A shoestring-friendly alternative: an intercity coach along the 132 corridor to Sainte-Anne-des-Monts. I have not verified the service frequency, the fare or the duration. There is also no confirmed onward link from Sainte-Anne-des-Monts into the park, so the last 40 km is unaccounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Backcountry hut (refuge) on the park's hut network
candidatesAccepted.summary: A rustic hut, the shelter you asked for, at a night's walk from the road and within your 16 km limit. I have not checked specific huts, availability or fords on approach trails. Pick huts on well-marked trails below exposed summits in case of cloud, and confirm current trail and ford conditions with the park. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Gîte du Mont-Albert, a lodge at the park's road access
candidatesAccepted.summary: A comfortable lodge at the park's main road access, useful as a road-side night if the hut nights fall short of four days. It is pricier than shoestring, and I have not verified current rates or access features.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont-Albert sector campground
candidatesAccepted.summary: A cheap, road-accessible tent site near the trailheads that suits a shoestring budget, as a night next to the road. I have not checked its season, site availability or accessibility.

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel in Sainte-Anne-des-Monts
candidatesAccepted.summary: A budget roof in the nearest town on the coast, a fallback if park lodging is full or the weather turns. I have not checked specific motels, rates or accessibility.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier summit hike
candidatesAccepted.summary: Classic alpine-tundra summit in the McGerrigle massif with caribou habitat; well-marked trail suits a pair who prefer not to navigate in cloud. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for; summit access can be restricted seasonally for caribou protection, so check current Sépaq rules.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Albert summit plateau hike
candidatesAccepted.summary: Demanding climb onto a serpentine tableland plateau with sweeping views; strenuous but on a marked trail. Exposed above treeline, so poor visibility matters given the party's wish to avoid cloud navigation. Access needs not answered and not accounted for.

place.name: Mont Albert trail, Gîte du Mont-Albert sector

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Xalibu and Lac aux Américains
candidatesAccepted.summary: Shorter, steep hike past a glacial cirque lake to an alpine summit; a good lower-commitment option if cloud rolls in on a bigger day. Access needs not answered and not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Overnight in a backcountry refuge hut
candidatesAccepted.summary: Rustic Sépaq refuges let the pair string together hut nights within their 16 km daily limit; huts fill in late summer, so reserve ahead. Ford depths on connecting trails were not checked against their above-the-knee limit, and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Albert summit plateau: exposure and cloud check
candidatesAccepted.summary: The Albert tableland is open, above-treeline terrain where cloud and wind can arrive quickly. Late August to mid-September brings cooler temperatures, frequent fog and the chance of near-freezing nights. Since neither of you has navigated in cloud, treat it as a weather-dependent option and have a below-treeline alternative ready. Carry a map, compass and GPS, a full shell, an insulating layer, a hat and gloves. Check the daily forecast and trail status with Sépaq at the Gîte du Mont-Albert discovery centre; this is not clearance. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for here.

candidatesAccepted.title: Backcountry huts: rustic shelter and kit
candidatesAccepted.summary: The park's refuges suit your rustic limit. You would need to bring your own sleeping bag rated for near-freezing, a stove and fuel, a water filter, and food for all three nights. Hut availability and reservation rules come from Sépaq; confirm with them. Late-summer demand is real, so book early.

place.name: Parc national de la Gaspésie backcountry refuges

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier: caribou closure and weather
candidatesAccepted.summary: This is a high, exposed summit where cloud and wind are frequent. Access may be restricted to protect the Gaspésie caribou herd, and in recent years it has been closed or limited. Check its current status with Sépaq before counting on it; nothing here confirms that it is open.

candidatesAccepted.title: Stream crossings and trail mud after rain
candidatesAccepted.summary: Most of the park's maintained trails cross streams on bridges, but heavy rain can raise brooks and flood low sections. Ask Sépaq staff about current crossing conditions so you can rule out any route with a ford above the knee. Waterproof boots and gaiters will help. River levels after rain were not accounted for here.

candidatesAccepted.title: Backcountry hut reservations through Sépaq
candidatesAccepted.summary: Three hut nights in the Chic-Chocs (refuges on the International Appalachian Trail / Mont-Albert sector) must be reserved ahead; late-summer weekends fill early. Choose huts within 16 km of each other on marked trails, and favour routes that stay below the open alpine plateaus, which matters if cloud comes in. Ford depths on hut routes were not checked; ask Sépaq when booking.

place.name: Sépaq reservations, Parc national de la Gaspésie

candidatesAccepted.title: Park access fee and backcountry registration
candidatesAccepted.summary: A daily park access fee applies for each person, and overnight hikers register their route at the Discovery and Visitors Centre before setting out. Registration gives staff a record of where you are expected; it is not a safety clearance. Ask about current trail closures, including any seasonal caribou-protection closures on summits.

place.name: Centre de découverte et de services

candidatesAccepted.title: Offline maps and a satellite messenger
candidatesAccepted.summary: There is essentially no cell coverage on the hut routes. Download offline topographic maps with GPS tracks before you go, so that following the trail in cloud depends less on navigation skill. Carry a rented or borrowed satellite messenger to call for help. I did not verify rental availability in Québec City.

candidatesAccepted.title: Check insurance covers backcountry rescue
candidatesAccepted.summary: Check that your health or travel insurance covers search, rescue and evacuation from remote terrain, especially if either of you lives outside Québec. Your access needs were not answered, so nothing here takes them into account.

gaps.detail: This part of the plan was left out to keep the run inside its budget. Re-planning with a larger budget would fill it in.
Nothing was checked about where to eat.
